newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem has potential buyers for units.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem has potential buyers for units.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp has had a "good level of interest" in the business units it wants to sell and has entered into confidentiality agreements with potential buyers, Chairman Curtis "Hank" Barnette said on Wednesday.
Barnette declined to name the interested parties.

"We are going to make every effort to sell these businesses," he told reporters in a conference call. "We have had a good level of interest...we have entered into confidentiality agreements with a number of potential buyers."

The company today announced plans to sell four unprofitable business units -- Bethlehem Structural Products Corp's Structural Mill, BethForge Inc, CENTEC Roll Corp and BethShip Inc's Sparrows Point Yard.
None of the four belongs to Bethlehem's core business of flat-rolled steel production.

The company said that if the businesses could not be sold in a "scheduled period of time," they would be shut down and efforts to sell them would continue. It did not specify what the "scheduled period" was.
Barnette also declined to be specific about a time frame but said the units would continue to operate into early 1997.
"We will evaluate the situation in early 1997," he said. "We want to see these businesses continue, we want to see jobs preserved."
As a result of the restructuring plan, Bethlehem said it would record an after-tax charge of about $375 million in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The units to be sold represent less than 10 percent of the company's total revenues.
